text: Define a database management system and state four advantages of using a DBMS instead of a file-processing system.
Describe the three-schema architecture of a database system. Explain logical data independence and physical data independence.
Draw an ER diagram for a hospital management system with patients, doctors, appointments and wards. Show all cardinality constraints.
Write relational algebra expressions to retrieve the names of employees who work in the Research department and earn more than 40000.
What is a B+ tree index? Compare a dense index with a sparse index in terms of storage and lookup cost.
Explain the two-phase locking protocol. Show with a schedule how strict 2PL avoids cascading rollback.
State the ACID properties of a transaction and explain each one with an appropriate example.
Given Employee(emp_id, project_id, hours, emp_name, dept_name, dept_head) with the given functional dependencies, normalise the relation up to 3NF showing every intermediate relation.
Map the given ER diagram into relational schemas and identify the primary key and foreign key of each resulting relation.
Using the schema Student(id, name, dept, cgpa), write SQL queries to list the top five students by CGPA and to count the number of students in each department.
Differentiate between conflict serializability and view serializability with examples.
Explain the ARIES recovery algorithm. What is the role of the write-ahead logging protocol in it?
What is data independence? Explain the three levels of abstraction used in a DBMS with a neat diagram.
Explain the difference between a candidate key, a super key and a foreign key with examples from a library database.
A query joins three large relations. Evaluate two alternative query plans and justify which one the optimiser should choose based on estimated cost.
Write SQL statements to create a table with appropriate constraints and to find students who have never enrolled in any course.
Explain deadlock in a database system. Describe wait-die and wound-wait deadlock prevention schemes.
Draw an ER diagram for an online bookstore and convert it into a normalised relational schema.
List and explain the responsibilities of a database administrator.
Define functional dependency. Compute the closure of the given attribute set and identify all candidate keys of the relation.
Explain hashing-based indexing. When would you prefer a hash index over a B+ tree index for a given workload?
What is a transaction? Explain the states in the transaction state diagram.
Write SQL queries using GROUP BY and HAVING to report the average grade per course for courses with more than twenty enrolled students.
Explain BCNF. Show that a relation in 3NF need not be in BCNF using a counter-example.
